Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held bilateral talks with his Polish counterpart, Donald Tusk,
in New Delhi.
During their talks, both leaders reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral relations
and also exchanged views on regional and global issues of mutual interest.
Addressing the joint press meet, Prime Minister Modi said the world is undergoing a
period of uncertainty and transformation, and despite these challenges,
India and Poland are emerging as important centres of growth, technology and innovation.
He said today both nations have agreed to boost cooperation in areas of defence, space
and nuclear energy.
Mr Modi invited companies from Poland to engage in co-development and co-production
with India in all these strategic sectors.

Mr Modi said the Indo-European Union Free Trade Agreement has created new opportunities

The Prime Minister said they also held detailed discussions on regional and global developments.
He said both India and Poland believe in democratic values and the rule of law.
Mr Modi said both countries believe that reforms are necessary to make global governance
institutions stronger and more effective. He said whether it is Ukraine or West Asia,
India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace.
Prime Minister Modi said the two nations also agreed to establish the
India-Poland startup bridge. He said these initiatives will give fresh momentum to cooperation
in AI, cyber, fintech and other emerging technologies.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah today inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for projects
worth over 8,941 crore rupees related to the rejuvenation of the Yamuna River.
river. The expansion of sewer networks and improvements to the drainage system mark significant
steps towards cleaning the Yamuna River. Speaking on the occasion, the Home Minister said the
BJP government is committed to cleaning and rejuvenating the Yamuna by May 2029. He said
the centre and the governments of Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh had prepared coordinated
time-bound action plans to tackle pollution in the river. Mr. Shah accused the previous
Ahmadmi Party government of making excuses instead of addressing the issue.
He reiterated that cleaning and rejuvenating the Yamuna remained a firm commitment of the
BJP government.
The minister said the projects inaugurated and launched today will strengthen wastewater
treatment, improve drinking water facilities and expand sewer connectivity across Delhi.
These projects serve as the backbone for the cleaning of Yamuna.

his vision for cleaning the Yamuna to the Delhi government and the Ministry of Home
Affairs.

in such a short time."

Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers JP Nadda has said India aims to develop a $1 trillion
chemicals market by 2040, inaugurating the 14th edition of India Chem 2026 at the Bombay
Exhibition Centre, Nesco, in Mumbai today. He said a favorable environment is emerging
in the country for the growth of the chemicals and petrochemicals sector. He added that
clear policies, government support, and positive industry participation are opening up new
opportunities for investment and growth in the sector.
Mr. Nadda said under the government's proposed Bhavira science scheme, the centre would
provide 1,000 crore rupees for each chemical park, while the concerned state would have
to contribute a minimum of 500 crore rupees.
He said the development of world-class infrastructure including port, rail, air
and road connectivity would be crucial to the selection and success of these parks.
President Ovidi Murmur released a commemorative 200 rupee coin to mark the 200th birth anniversary
of Puja Mata Saheb Hasi Devi ji at Lokbhavan in Rajpur, Chhattisgarh today.
Hundreds of members of the Sindhi community attended the event. Puja Mata Hasi Devi
ji was the fifth head of the historic Shraddhani Darbar, a revered spiritual and cultural
Central Centre for the Sindhi Community.
Following this program, President Murmur will attend the Seva Sammanparv and Yuvav Prabodhan
events at the Sardar Balbir Singh Junaidha indoor stadium in Raipur as part of the Nuhakhai
celebrations.
Education Minister Pallar Joshi today launched the portal for Kashi Tamil Sangamom 5.0,
which will be held in Varanasi from the 28th of November to the 12th of December this
year.
The theme of this edition is Tirukurel by Ilwam. Let us learn the Tirukurel.
In a social media post, Mr Joshi said the event will bring together over 1,400 delegates across seven categories.
He added that a special initiative involving 1,000 students from 1,000 higher educational institutions
will further deepen engagement with the timeless wisdom of the Tirukurel
and strengthen India's shared cultural heritage.
Union Agriculture and Farmers, well-feminist Shivrath Singh Chauhan, will launch the nationwide
Ketbachawabhyan Rabi 2026 from Karnal in Haryana today.
The campaign will continue until November 30th.
The initiative is aimed at promoting sustainable agriculture, improving soil health, and encouraging
the judicious use of agricultural resources.
The campaign aims to create awareness among farmers about the balanced and judicious
use of fertilizers and other agricultural inputs based on soil testing. It will promote
crop diversification through oil seed, pulse and horticulture missions, encourage the
effective utilization of fallow fields after paddy harvesting and promote proper crop
residue management.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal today said 1.3 metric tons of Sindhuri
pomegranates from Kullu, Himachal Pradesh have been exported to Dubai with the
support of agricultural and processed food products export development authority APDA.
In a social media post, Mr. Goel said the produce of farmers from the state is now gaining a
new identity in global markets. He noted that this initiative to connect local produce
with global markets is an important step towards increasing farmers' income and taking
Indian agricultural exports to new heights.
The Election Commission has announced by poll to one seat of the Rajya Sabha in Madhya Pradesh.
The seat is vacant due to the resignation of BJP leader and former Union Minister Dr.
L. Murugan.
The nomination will begin on the 26th of this month and polling will be held on the 12th
of November.

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh today said one international was killed and two sustained
injuries in the Dhammam Airport attack last night.
In a social media post, the Indian Embassy said it is ascertaining further details in
contacting the affected families.
It also extended prayers to the family and loved ones of the deceased and wished
for the recovery of the injured.
The Minister of Boats, Shipping and Waterways, Sarban and Sonowal, has said all 21 Indian
crew members along with the rest of the crew on board a Kuwait flagged oil product tanker
are safe after the vessel was struck by an unknown projectile.
In a social media post, Mr Sonowal said the incident occurred yesterday while the
ship empty Aldasma was transiting through the Strait of Hormuz.
He said India is closely monitoring the situation and remains in contact with the ship management
management company to ensure the ongoing security and well-being of the seafarers.
Tensions between the United States and Iran have escalated amid reports of preparations
for possible renewed military strikes against Tehran.
U.S. President Donald Trump has indicated that developments could come soon, but said Washington
is not currently negotiating with Iran.
Iran has warned of retaliation against any renewed attacks.
The media report said Washington was deploying additional military assets to the region while
the possibility of strikes could also be used as leverage in negotiations over Iran's nuclear
program and control of the state of Hormuz.
The United Nations has warned that a powerful El Nino could trigger major economic shocks
worldwide with Latin America, Africa, Asia, and the Pacific facing extreme heat, droughts
and floods.
Speaking at a news conference in Geneva, UN Undersecretary General Tom Fletcher described
the phenomenon as a wrecking ball and called for urgent global action to minimize its impact.
Mr Fletcher warned that the consequences could extend beyond affected regions, fueling conflict,
displacement and migration, while meteorological organization chief Celeste Saulo said El
Nino could reach unprecedented strength towards the end of this year with its effect continuing
long afterwards.
